journey.name: A session Loopky cannot reach — recovery, honest copy, and a way out
journey.description:
Every authenticated write opens with `POST https://_pubky.<pubky>/session`. On device that round trip starts failing after an hour or so and takes the whole write path with it while reads keep working (#165). Three things were wrong with how the app met that:
1. nothing retried it, so the app parked there until a manual sign-out/sign-in; 2. the FFI's wording matched `isNetworkFailure`, so publish said "check your connection" about a connection that was measurably fine; 3. the deck editor rendered the throwable's own message — `Failed to import session: Request failed: HTTP transport error: error sending request for url (…/session)` — in place of the card list, the only place the real cause appeared at all.
Reproducing the real thing means waiting an hour, so drive it with a fault injection instead. In `AndroidPubkyClient`, make the three `*WithSession` writes return, after the first dozen calls, `PubkyError("Failed to import session: Request failed: HTTP transport error: error sending request for url (https://_pubky.rc3omrqq/session)")` — that exact wording is what the classifier keys on. Letting the first calls through leaves one signed-in run able to publish a real deck first. **Revert the injection before committing.**
Requires a signed-in session (journey 01, or restore per journey 20).

actions.action: With the injection built in, publish a small deck from Paste-to-Import — it must succeed, so the later failures are the wedge and not a broken build
Open the deck → Edit deck → Save, repeating until logcat shows `Loopky/DeckEditorVM: save: FAILED`
Verify logcat shows `Loopky/SessionRevalidator: revalidating session` between the two write attempts — the write is retried once through a fresh session import, not reported on the first failure
Scroll the editor to the foot of the card list and verify the error reads "Couldn't save this deck. Loopky couldn't re-establish your session. It's not your connection — try again."
Verify the error contains no URL, no "HTTP transport error", and no other FFI diagnostic text
Verify the copy does NOT tell the user to check their connection — that is the offline message, and this is not offline
Verify an element with resource-id "deck_editor_sign_in_again" is present below the message
Tap it and verify the app signs out and lands on the onboarding screen
Sign in again, then repeat the failure on the publish flow: Paste-to-Import → triage → Publish deck
Verify the publish error reads "Couldn't publish this deck." followed by the same session copy, and that "publish_sign_in_again" is offered beside it

Repeat the editor check on the Pixel_Tablet AVD in both orientations (`user_rotation 0` = expanded 1280dp, `1` = medium 800dp) — the error row is inside the editor's `contentPane(Reading)` column and must stay capped with the cards, not stretch the width of the pane
